name: cxfrs
title: CXF-RS
description: Expose JAX-RS REST services using Apache CXF or connect to external REST services using CXF REST client.
label: rest

properties.name: beanId
properties.description: To lookup an existing configured CxfRsEndpoint. Must used bean: as prefix.

properties.name: address
properties.description: The service publish address.

properties.name: features
properties.description: Set the feature list to the CxfRs endpoint.

properties.name: modelRef
properties.description: This option is used to specify the model file which is useful for the resource class without annotation. When using this option, then the service class can be omitted, to emulate document-only endpoints

properties.name: providers
properties.description: Set custom JAX-RS provider(s) list to the CxfRs endpoint. You can specify a string with a list of providers to lookup in the registy separated by comma.

properties.name: resourceClasses
properties.description: The resource classes which you want to export as REST service. Multiple classes can be separated by comma.

properties.name: schemaLocations
properties.description: Sets the locations of the schema(s) which can be used to validate the incoming XML or JAXB-driven JSON.

properties.name: skipFaultLogging
properties.description: This option controls whether the PhaseInterceptorChain skips logging the Fault that it catches.

properties.name: bindingStyle
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Sets how requests and responses will be mapped to/from Camel. Two values are possible: SimpleConsumer: This binding style processes request parameters, multiparts, etc. and maps them to IN headers, IN attachments and to the message body. It aims to eliminate low-level processing of org.apache.cxf.message.MessageContentsList. It also also adds more flexibility and simplicity to the response mapping. Only available for consumers. Default: The default style. For consumers this passes on a MessageContentsList to the route, requiring low-level processing in the route. This is the traditional binding style, which simply dumps the org.apache.cxf.message.MessageContentsList coming in from the CXF stack onto the IN message body. The user is then responsible for processing it according to the contract defined by the JAX-RS method signature. Custom: allows you to specify a custom binding through the binding option.

properties.name: publishedEndpointUrl
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: This option can override the endpointUrl that published from the WADL which can be accessed with resource address url plus _wadl

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: serviceBeans
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: The service beans (the bean ids to lookup in the registry) which you want to export as REST service. Multiple beans can be separated by comma

properties.name: cookieHandler
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Configure a cookie handler to maintain a HTTP session

properties.name: hostnameVerifier
properties.label: producer
properties.description: The hostname verifier to be used. Use the # notation to reference a HostnameVerifier from the registry.

properties.name: sslContextParameters
properties.label: producer
properties.description: The Camel SSL setting reference. Use the # notation to reference the SSL Context.

properties.name: throwExceptionOnFailure
properties.label: producer
properties.description: This option tells the CxfRsProducer to inspect return codes and will generate an Exception if the return code is larger than 207.

properties.name: httpClientAPI
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: If it is true, the CxfRsProducer will use the HttpClientAPI to invoke the service. If it is false, the CxfRsProducer will use the ProxyClientAPI to invoke the service

properties.name: ignoreDeleteMethodMessageBody
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: This option is used to tell CxfRsProducer to ignore the message body of the DELETE method when using HTTP API.

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: maxClientCacheSize
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: This option allows you to configure the maximum size of the cache. The implementation caches CXF clients or ClientFactoryBean in CxfProvider and CxfRsProvider. The value must be greater than 0.

properties.name: synchronous
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Sets whether synchronous processing should be strictly used

properties.name: binding
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use a custom CxfBinding to control the binding between Camel Message and CXF Message.

properties.name: bus
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use a custom configured CXF Bus.

properties.name: continuationTimeout
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: This option is used to set the CXF continuation timeout which could be used in CxfConsumer by default when the CXF server is using Jetty or Servlet transport.

properties.name: cxfRsConfigurer
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: This option could apply the implementation of org.apache.camel.component.cxf.jaxrs.CxfRsEndpointConfigurer which supports to configure the CXF endpoint in programmatic way. User can configure the CXF server and client by implementing configure{Server/Client} method of CxfEndpointConfigurer.

properties.name: defaultBus
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Will set the default bus when CXF endpoint create a bus by itself

properties.name: headerFilterStrategy
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter header to and from Camel message.

properties.name: performInvocation
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: When the option is true, Camel will perform the invocation of the resource class instance and put the response object into the exchange for further processing.

properties.name: propagateContexts
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: When the option is true, JAXRS UriInfo, HttpHeaders, Request and SecurityContext contexts will be available to custom CXFRS processors as typed Camel exchange properties. These contexts can be used to analyze the current requests using JAX-RS API.

properties.name: loggingFeatureEnabled
properties.label: logging
properties.description: This option enables CXF Logging Feature which writes inbound and outbound REST messages to log.

properties.name: loggingSizeLimit
properties.label: logging
properties.description: To limit the total size of number of bytes the logger will output when logging feature has been enabled and -1 for no limit.
